sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cloud Vulnerability Scanning and Penetration Testing SaaS

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic Code heritage with German-influenced commercial company statutes; codified, with judicial precedent as persuasive authority)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: BLEU–China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 5 June 2005, in force 1 December 2009)
Luxembourg–United States Double Tax Treaty (Convention of 3 April 1996, as amended by Protocol of 24 May 2009)
Luxembourg–Germany Double Tax Treaty (2012, replacing the 1958 Convention)
Luxembourg–France Double Tax Treaty (Convention of 1 April 1958, as amended)
OECD Multilateral Instrument (MLI) applicable to Luxembourg's tax treaty network

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Loi du 12 novembre 2004 sur la lutte contre le blanchiment et le financement du terrorisme, as amended (AML/CFT Law); Loi du 13 janvier 2019 instituant un Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (UBO Register Law); Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, Articles 61-1 et seq. (SCSp regime introduced by the Law of 23 July 2016); CSSF Circulars 17/650 and 20/744; RBE implementing regulations of 1 February 2019.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized certified copy of passport of each natural-person UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary of the UBO's country of origin (or Luxembourg notary for in-country signatories)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization (non-Hague jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (recent utility bill or bank statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or financial institution in country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy, with Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization where the original is foreign

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation / certificate of good standing of any foreign corporate General Partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or competent commercial registrar of the foreign jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization (non-Hague jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board resolution (or equivalent written consent) of the corporate General Partner approving SCSp formation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the corporate General Partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized certification, then Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified English/French/German translation of all non-language-compliant corporate documents
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Sworn translator (traducteur assermenté) listed with the Luxembourg Ministry of Justice
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certificate of the sworn translator attached to the translated deed (no apostille required for the translation itself)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP, sanctions and adverse-media screening against: Luxembourg FIU (Cellule de Renseignement Financier) AML bulletins; EU Council Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (CFSP); UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; OFAC SDN list (applied as bank/counterparty KYC policy); FATF public statements and grey-list status; CSSF AML/CFT guidance. Screening is conducted at formation, before each capital movement, and on an ongoing transaction-monitoring basis.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — electronic filing platform for the RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés), www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names may be registered in Luxembourgish, French, German, English or another Latin-alphabet language. Non-Latin scripts must be romanized/transliterated into the Latin alphabet. The name must be sufficiently distinctive, contain a legal-form identifier (e.g., 'SCSp' or 'Société en Commandite Spéciale'), and must not mislead as to the company's activity. No nationwide registered trademark search is performed by the RCS ex officio; counsel should run EUIPO/INPI clearance in parallel.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: SICAV / SICAF / Fonds de placement / OPC / UCITS (requires CSSF authorization)
SPF / Société de participation financière (special-status holding company)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection by the RCS registrar, counsel may immediately re-file a corrected name reservation in the same LBR queue. A formal administrative review may be requested from the RCS registrar at the Luxembourg Business Registers. If the refusal is maintained, the applicant may appeal to the President of the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg) in summary proceedings under Article 44 of the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the RCS. Strategically, counsel should parallel-reserve an alternative name and validate EUIPO trademark availability to avoid commercial delay.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted. The SCSp must maintain a registered office (siège) in Luxembourg; a licensed domiciliation agent may supply the address and assume statutory service duties. The arrangement is not treated as a 'virtual office' in the AML sense where the domiciliation agent performs regulatory KYC. A fully remote operating model is acceptable for ISIC 6201 SaaS, provided the company can demonstrate substantive management, bank connectivity, accounting records and org structure in Luxembourg (ATAD/exit substance parameters).
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low — approximately 3–5% cumulative risk over a 3-year horizon. Unannounced physical inspections are uncommon for an unleveraged, non-regulated cybersecurity SaaS vehicle; the Luxembourg tax administration (Administration des contributions directes) more frequently conducts documentary substance audits, and the CSSF would only assert inspection rights if the entity later becomes regulated.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory RCS tariff (electronically filed; no counsel surcharge)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Drafting of SCSp partnership agreement (private deed or notarial-form corporate documents)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark flat fee, EUR 3,000–5,000 for a standard SCSp (excl. VAT)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial authentication of the deed (optional but recommended for bank onboarding)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial tariff (émoluments) with economy-of-scale engagement; varies EUR 1,500–3,000

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS incorporation filing (Form C-1) and RESA electronic publication
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory RCS filing and publication tariff (electronic channel)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RBE (UBO register) registration and legal compliance support
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External counsel (RBE filing to LBR is statutorily free of charge)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark time-based fee for UBO declaration and ongoing filing support

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office / domiciliation setup and first-year service fee
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market standard, EUR 1,200–2,000 for the first year, plus statutory setup documentation

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation AML/KYC CDD of UBOs and general partner (PEP/sanctions/adverse-media screening)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark fixed fee for 3–5 natural persons and 1 corporate entity

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille / consular legalization of foreign identity and corporate documents (bundle of 5)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Governmental fee schedule of issuing authorities; excludes notarization in country of origin

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified translation of foreign corporate documents into French, German or English
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Court-approved translator tariff, per-page basis (estimated 5 pages)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Amended Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), as amended by the Law of 12 July 2013 introducing the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp); applicable provisions Articles 20-1 to 20-8 of the 1915 Law; supplementary RCS filing and publication regime under the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés - RCS), operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR); electronic filings through the eJustice.public.lu portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: SCSp Partnership Agreement / Constitutive Deed (Contrat de société / Acte de constitution), executed either as a notarized deed (acte notarié) or as a private writing (acte sous seing privé) with certified signatures; accompanied by the RCS incorporation e-form.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum capital and no escrow (blocage) account requirement for the SCSp. Contributions are freely fixed in the partnership agreement, may be cash, in-kind, or in industry/services for the general partner, and are payable per the agreed contribution schedule; registration does not require evidence of capital paid.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST RESOLUTION OF THE GENERAL PARTNER (MANAGEMENT). The general partner of [COMPANY] SCSp (the 'Partnership') hereby resolves: (i) to accept and record the subscription of capital commitments and contributions of the initial partners; (ii) to adopt the registered office at [●], Luxembourg, and to approve the domiciliation agreement; (iii) to appoint [NAME] as manager (gérant), with sole power to represent the Partnership vis-à-vis third parties; (iv) to instruct counsel to file the constitutive deed with the RCS and to procure publication in the RESA; (v) to open the Partnership's bank account and to complete VAT and social security registrations. This resolution takes effect immediately and shall be recorded in the minutes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of the SCSp Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg civil-law notary (recommended, not obligatory for SCSp) or legal counsel with certified signatures; final acceptance by partner(s).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare and execute the SCSp constitutive deed containing the corporate name with the 'SCSp' suffix, the corporate object restricted to cloud vulnerability scanning and penetration-testing SaaS (ISIC 6201 / NAICS 541512), registered office address, identity and capital commitments of the general partner and limited partners, management and representation clauses, fiscal year, and Luxembourg governing law. If executed as a private writing, all partner signatures must be certified or legalized to satisfy RCS acceptability; notarization is strongly advised to avoid registry queries.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or national ID of each partner
Draft SCSp partnership agreement (acte de constitution)
Declaration of corporate object and ISIC classification
Written acceptance of appointment by the general partner or manager
Extracts from criminal records (bulletin n°3) for appointing managers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary or counsel flags inconsistencies, execute an amending act (acte rectificatif) before filing; if a partner signature is defective, re-execute the signature page under notarial supervision.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of the Registered Office and Domiciliation Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Domiciliation service provider or landlord; municipal authority of the registered-office commune.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Secure a legal registered office in Luxembourg (Grand Duchy of Luxembourg). Sign either a lease with the landlord's written consent or a professional domiciliation agreement accepted by the RCS. Ensure the physical address is operational and that the general partner has legal authority to use the address at all times. Obtain the landlord's express consent to attach to the RCS registration file.
required_dossiers: Domiciliation agreement (contrat de domiciliation) or lease
Written consent of the registered-office owner (consentement du propriétaire)
Identity document of the domiciliation provider's legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS rejects the address for lack of proof, provide a notarially certified copy of the lease and an updated owner consent statement; alternatively transfer the registered office to an approved domiciliation agent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration Filing with the RCS via eJustice
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS) - eJustice.public.lu electronic filing portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Create an eJustice user account, select the RCS incorporation procedure, complete the standardized company information e-form, attach the constitutive deed and supporting documents, pay the statutory filing fee, and submit. The registering officer checks legal validity, name availability, object legality, and representative authority. Upon approval, the RCS issues the certificate of registration and the RCS extract (extrait du RCS), which stands as proof of incorporation of the SCSp.
required_dossiers: Executed constitutive deed (notarial or certified private deed)
RCS incorporation e-form (completed online)
Domiciliation agreement and landlord consent
Joined transcript of the general partner's resolution appointing the manager
Identity documents and criminal-record bulletins of the manager
Proof of payment of the RCS filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query (demande de renseignements), respond within the indicated peremptory time-limit via the eJustice file-exchange module, providing the missing annexes or a corrective deed; if the file is closed, re-submit with full compliance.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Mandatory Publication in the RESA (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS acting as depositary of the RESA; extracted electronically at resa.lu.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after RCS registration, the registrar automatically publishes the constitutive deed and the legal events of incorporation in the RESA. Verify the publication including the name form 'SCSp', the registered office, the object, and the identity of the legal representative; download the RESA publication receipt and the RCS registration extract for use with banks and counterparties.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
RESA publication receipt
Copy of the constitutive deed as deposited
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a published fact is inaccurate or incomplete, request a rectification from the RCS; in the case of a refusal, apply to the competent Tribunal d'arrondissement of Luxembourg for an order to correct the registered data.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT Registration with the Luxembourg Tax Authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) - business registration desk, acting through the guichet.lu / eCDF online portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, file the VAT form (N° 278) to register the SCSp as a taxable person. For cloud SaaS services, the place-of-supply rules for digital services apply; cross-border B2B supplies of cybersecurity SaaS are generally subject to reverse charge, while B2C digital supplies may attract the Luxembourg standard VAT rate. If projected annual turnover is below the EUR 30,000 small-business threshold, the exemption from VAT may be claimed; the taxable persons register will issue the LU VAT number.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Constitutive deed and RESA publication receipt
Bank account certificate or IBAN confirmation
Identity document of the manager or general partner
Declaration of projected turnover and activity commencement date
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT queries the file or requires additional information, respond through the electronic tax mailbox within the granted deadline; correct any misdeclaration of place of supply and, if necessary, apply for the small-business exemption in writing to avoid undue VAT registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Social Security, Employer, and Occupational Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS); Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM); municipal authority and Grand-Ducal Fire and Rescue Corps (CGDIS) where premises are occupied.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the SCSp as an employer with the CCSS if any staff are recruited, and file the first declaration of social security affiliation. For the physical workplace, ensure compliance with ITM occupational health and safety rules and municipal fire-safety requirements; for office-only activity, no industrial environmental permit is required. Open the payroll file and appoint an in-house safety delegate or external coordinator as required by the Labour Code.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Identity document of the legal representative
Copy of employment contracts (if any)
Fire-safety and structural-conformity files for the premises
CCSS employer registration form (formulaire de reconnaissance employeur)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CCSS or ITM issues a query or an infringement notice, correct the social declarations and produce a remediation plan for workplace or fire-safety deficits; re-submit the fire-safety dossier to the municipal commission after remedial works are certified.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — office-based ISIC 6201 cybersecurity SaaS is not an industrial pursuit requiring an industrial establishment permit. Reference authority for regulated professions (none triggered): Ministry of the Economy — Directorate-General for SMEs and Digitalisation (autorisation d'établissement regime).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No operating license (autorisation d'établissement) is required for cloud vulnerability scanning and penetration-testing SaaS; the profession is not listed as a regulated trade, craft, or retail activity under the amended Law of 2 September 2011 on access to professions.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt / Class 0 — office-based SaaS activity does not fall under Appendix V of the amended Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment, nor under the environmental licensing regime for installations (établissements classés).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater discharge, VOC, or combustion thresholds apply. Office-generic municipal wastewater must comply with municipal sanitary ordinances; waste electrical and electronic equipment (WEEE), batteries, and packaging must be delivered to a registered national compliance scheme (e.g., Ecotrel) under the amended Law of 21 March 2012 on waste management; hazardous office waste must be handled by licensed waste carriers.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety conformity certificate for office premises issued by the municipal authority after joint inspection with the Grand-Ducal Fire and Rescue Corps (CGDIS), including escape-route plans and fire-extinguisher maintenance; occupational safety registration with the ITM covering electrical installations, VDU workstation compliance, and, where staff are engaged, a health-and-safety coordination dossier, first-aid provisions, and accident declaration protocols.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD), the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration, for corporate and municipal business tax; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT and indirect tax registration. Primary digital portals: MyGuichet.lu for entity registration and filings, eTVA for VAT returns, and the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Luxembourg SCSp obtains its national business matricule (11-digit statutory TIN) upon incorporation and registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers, effected through a notary or an authorized MyGuichet.lu filer. The AEDT subsequently issues the VAT identification number in the format LU plus 10 digits upon VAT registration or on commencement of taxable activity. Non-resident ownership is unrestricted and no minimum capital is required. A foreign entity not otherwise established in Luxembourg but making taxable supplies there applies directly to the AEDT for a VAT number, with no local turnover threshold; documentation required includes proof of identity of the promoters, description of the planned activity (ISIC/NACE), and evidence of foreign establishment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Default treatment: the SCSp is fiscally transparent; income, gains, deductions, and credits are allocated directly to partners, and no Luxembourg CIT or municipal business tax is levied at the entity level. Statutory options include (i) an opaque-taxation election under Article 175 LITL, as amended by the Law of 21 December 2017, permitting the partnership to elect to be assessed as a Luxembourg resident company for CIT and municipal business tax purposes, subject to anti-hybrid and ATAD constraints; (ii) an election to acquire legal personality under Articles 944-1 et seq. of the Law of 10 August 1915, converting the SCSp into a Société en commandite simple and thereby changing tax classification and treaty entitlement analysis; and (iii) the domestic Luxembourg anti-hybrid mismatch rules, which condition or deny double-dip outcomes in cross-border structures.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée) governed by the Law of 12 February 1979 on VAT (Loi TVA), implementing Council Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 in annual taxable turnover for Luxembourg-established suppliers under the small-business exemption in Article 57 Loi TVA; registration is compulsory once the threshold is exceeded or upon first taxable transaction. No registration threshold applies to non-established foreign suppliers, although supplies to Luxembourg VAT-registered customers may fall under the reverse-charge mechanism, and cross-border B2C digital services may be declared through the Union or non-Union OSS rather than through full local VAT registration.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, government API telemetry, or digital stamping requirement currently applies to B2B or B2C VAT in Luxembourg; paper and PDF invoices remain valid subject to the authenticity and integrity requirements of Articles 71 et seq. Loi TVA. B2G e-invoicing is mandatory for Luxembourg public procurement under the Law of 2 March 2022 transposing Directive 2014/55/EU, using the PEPPOL/EN 16931 format. Cross-border EU data exchange runs through the VIES framework; the EU ViDA initiative will progressively introduce standardized e-invoicing and digital reporting, but no national pre-clearance mandate exists today.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of cybersecurity SaaS services (cloud vulnerability scanning, penetration testing, and compliance software) by a Luxembourg supplier to a taxable customer established outside Luxembourg are subject to 0% Luxembourg VAT because the place of supply is the customer's country under Article 44 of Directive 2006/112/EC and Article 58 Loi TVA. Eligibility requires the supplier to obtain and validate the customer's EU VAT identification number for intra-Community B2B supplies, or to preserve written and commercial evidence of the customer's overseas establishment for non-EU customers; contracts, delivery reports, system/IP logs, payment routing, and service-use data must demonstrate that the services are not effectively enjoyed in Luxembourg. B2C supplies of digital services to non-resident consumers are taxable at the consumer's location via the OSS route, not in Luxembourg. Physical exports of goods would separately require customs export clearance; this does not apply to the pure SaaS service line.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration, Bill of Lading, Inward Remittance Certificate
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: An unjustified claim of the 0% rate is recharacterized as a Luxembourg taxable supply at 17% VAT. The AEDT may reassess within the statutory limitation period, which is extended in cases of fraud or intent, with statutory late-payment interest, forfeiture of input VAT credits, administrative fines under the Loi TVA penalty scale, and criminal prosecution, including fines and imprisonment, for willful evasion. The taxpayer bears the burden of proof; missing, contradictory, or untraceable substantiation, whether customs declarations, bills of lading, remittance certificates, or contractual and technical delivery evidence, invalidates the zero-rating and triggers retrospective clawback of VAT together with accumulated interest and penalties.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) — the Luxembourg central bank, operating within the Eurosystem and under the Single Supervisory Mechanism (SSM) for credit institutions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg maintains full convertibility on both current and capital account transactions. The euro is a freely floating convertible currency. No exchange control restrictions or prior approval requirements apply to outbound profit remittance, dividends, interest, or royalties, subject to EU/UN financial sanctions and the general anti-abuse rules. Non-resident shareholders may freely receive distributions from a Luxembourg SCSp, and applicable withholding taxes are mitigated by the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive and tax treaties.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender or mandatory repatriation requirement exists under Luxembourg law. Exporters may retain foreign currency balances indefinitely and convert them as needed at market rates.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low-to-Medium for strategic treasury use. EEA-authorised Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) and Payment Institutions can passport into Luxembourg under PSD2 and may provide an operational payment account for a SCSp. However, offshore digital EMIs outside the EU/EEA cannot passport, and UK-licensed EMIs have lost EU passporting rights post-Brexit. Legal constraints include limited credit/lending powers, lack of deposit-guarantee protection, and restrictiveness for capital escrow, FX hedging, and high-value trade settlement. Such EMIs are acceptable only for low-value subscription collection and non-critical disbursements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required for the initial AML/KYC interview at Luxembourg tier-1 banks, though remote video identification is permissible under CSSF regulations in strictly controlled circumstances. For a partnership such as the SCSp, banks normally require at least one physical meeting with the general partner and ultimate beneficial owner(s), or a notarised/certified identity verification performed by a recognised intermediary. In practice, onboarding can be conducted through a hybrid flow: remote document submission followed by video-call identity verification and a notarised confirmation from a Luxembourg-based agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex or opaque ultimate beneficial ownership structure, typical for SCSp with corporate general partner and layered investors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Updated LBR (Luxembourg Business Registers) UBO extract, full chain-of-ownership diagram, constitutional documents, partnership agreement (SCSp agreement), resolution of general partner approving account opening, passport copies of all UBOs, and proof of address.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of wealth / source of funds for the initial contemporaneous capital contribution from SaaS founders or overseas technology investors
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed and dated source-of-wealth questionnaire, latest personal bank statements, tax assessments, completed audit trail for the capital contribution, investment agreement, certificate of incorporation of contributing entity, and valuation documentation for any crypto or equity disposals.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Potential exposure to sanctions, PEP status, or high-risk jurisdictions through non-resident partners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Negative media and sanctions-screening reports, PEP declaration forms, proof of economic substance, source-of-wealth evidence from regulated financial institutions, and a standalone legal representation letter confirming no nexus with restricted jurisdictions or designated persons.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear business purpose versus expected transaction patterns, especially mixed subscription revenues and capital deployment
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business plan, treasury policy, executed B2B customer contracts for cloud vulnerability scanning and penetration testing, projected cash-flow model, evidence of Stripe merchant account history, detailed description of SWIFT purpose codes to be used, and a clearing-rails onboarding letter from the bank.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound routing is executed via SWIFT MT103 or SEPA Credit Transfer using an appropriate EBA BOP purpose code such as 'D020' for capital contributions or 'S001' for general working capital. The ordering party's name, address, account number, and, where applicable, LEI must be transmitted per Regulation (EU) 2015/847 on information accompanying transfers. The beneficiary SCSp must provide the bank with the partnership agreement, inward capital confirmation, UBO declaration, and a board/general-partner resolution to allow credit into the Capital Escrow Account. Any conversion from foreign currency is conducted at prevailing market rates.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound settlements are cleared through SWIFT MT103 for direct vendor payments and through Commercial Letters of Credit (ICC UCP 600) with SWIFT MT700/MT799 for high-value trade-backed procurements. For euro-area counterparties, SEPA Credit Transfer with mandatory structured remittance data is the default low-cost rail. All outbound wires require tax-compliant Beneficial Ownership declarations (due diligence), invoices, and proof-of-delivery where needed. Luxembourg does not impose surrender or conversion requirements on foreign-currency disbursements, allowing the SCSp to time FX execution freely.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Plain vanilla OTC FX forwards in major convertible pairs (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, EUR/CHF)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or illiquid emerging-market currencies
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) under an ISDA Master Agreement, subject to EMIR clearing and margining thresholds
European-style FX options on major pairs, permitted for risk management of subscription revenue and capex commitments

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of registration details (confirmation annuelle) with the RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) via the eJustice portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary-based: due by the last day of the month corresponding to the RCS registration anniversary (e.g., 31 March for a 15 March incorporation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late surcharge applied at filing; a second consecutive missed confirmation triggers a formal warning and administrative strike-off (radiation) proceedings with dissolution risk

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owner data in the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-based: at least one confirmation mandatory per calendar year; beneficial-owner changes (e.g., partnership interest transfers) must be filed within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to EUR 5,000 (USD 5,450); deliberate non-disclosure risks criminal fines of EUR 1,250–1,250,000 (USD 1,360–1,362,500) and imprisonment from 6 months to 5 years; issuance of RCS compliance certificates is blocked

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual accounts (dépôt des comptes annuels) when the SCSp is not validly exempted
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: RCS via eJustice (publication in the Luxembourg Business Registers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of the financial year-end; RCS filing due within one month after formal approval of the accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge plus criminal fine of EUR 500–5,000 (USD 545–5,450); persistent default can trigger compulsory audit and administrative strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if two of the three thresholds are exceeded for two consecutive years: balance-sheet total > EUR 6.25M, net turnover > EUR 12.5M, average workforce > 250; SCSp vehicles whose partners are exclusively legal entities are generally exempt from audit
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP (Law of 19 December 2002 as amended; EU Accounting Directive 2013/34/EU); IFRS permitted for unlisted entities and mandatory for consolidated accounts of listed groups

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The general partner must maintain an accurate register of limited partners and beneficial owners; any transfer or pledge of partnership interests must be filed in the RBE within 30 days; an annual no-change confirmation must still be validated to keep the entity in good standing, and RCS certificate issuance is suspended for non-compliant entities
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of limited partners (held by the general partner)
Minute book of resolutions of the general partner and partner meetings
Accounting books, vouchers and correspondence (10-year retention)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 4,000 – 10,000 (EUR 3,670 – 9,170) when the exemption is unavailable; EUR 0 when the all-legal-entity-partners exemption applies
